Wash soil from all farm tools and boots and disinfect using approved chlorine-based products when moving from an infected area.
Ensure that the pH of the soil is above 7 by adding lime.
Monitoring: Look on leaves for yellowing around margins that progresses from the older to younger leaves leading to the willting of the whole plant.
Look for leaves of infected plants which collapse and sag towards the pseudostem sometimes with the top leaf remaining upright.
Cut a cross-section of infected pseudostems and check for pale yellow, dark red or brownish colouration.
Monitor crop at least every 2 weeks and take action immediately if an infected plant is detected.
Direct Control: An infected plant should be killed in situ.
Do not dig out the plant or chop the plant into pieces.
Kill it with a herbicide injection.

Before use, read and follow pesticide product label instructions e.g.
PHI, REI, usage and disposal of pesticide waste.
Do not empty pesticides into drains.
Always seek technical assistance before use of pesticide.
No synthetic chemicals are registered against fusarium wilt on banana.
However, effective chemicals registered against fusarium wilt on other crops may be used with caution.
Before planting, dip seedlings stools in carbendazim-based products as a prophylactic measure.
U (unlikely to present hazard under conditions of normal use).
